boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Big Bethel record (June 10, 1861) in Blockade of the Chesapeake Bay [May-June 1861]. The night march from Hampton and Newport News, the destruction of Little Bethel and the pursuit to New Market Bridge are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 4,700 (US 3,500; CS 1,200). Magruder reports about 3,500 attackers (prisoners said 5,000) and his own force about 1,200 engaged and 1,400 in all, 'about one thousand two hundred men' all told. Pierce says Duryea crossed with some 850 men and Townsend followed with 650, and that a woman at a farm-house said Big Bethel was garrisoned by some 4,000.
claims.rationale: Point figures from the Confederate commander's dispatches and partial regimental figures from Pierce; the frozen figures resemble Magruder's but their basis is not established. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: NPS says the Confederates fell back to entrenchments behind Brick Kiln Creek near Big Bethel Church. Pierce found the enemy in a strong position in battery at the head of the road, and the Newport News troops were prevented from charging by a creek. Magruder mentions a precipice over which a disabled gun was thrown and a house in front that was thought to cover the enemy.
claims.rationale: Ground from a summary and the two reports; no map inspected. NPS calls them entrenchments to which the Confederates fell back; the inspected passages do not date their construction.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel John B. Magruder and Colonel D.H. Hill for the Confederates and Brigadier General Ebenezer Pierce for the Union; the live page gives Magruder as Major General, and he signs as colonel commanding the Hampton Division. NPS says the Federals were under Pierce's immediate command. Pierce says he decided to follow his written instructions against his colonels' advice and later directed all forces to retire; Magruder praises Hill's 'judicious and determined action'.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a summary and the two reports; no listed commander receives automatic sole credit and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Magruder says the enemy was repulsed at all points and totally routed after two hours and a half; Pierce says it became apparent the battery had been strongly reinforced and any effort to take it useless, and he directed a retreat covered by two fresh regiments; NPS says the Union forces were disorganized and retired.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 87 (US 79; CS 8); the live field reads 84 (US 76; CS 8), and NPS gives Confederate losses of 1 killed and 7 wounded. Magruder reports his own loss as one killed and seven wounded; for the enemy, ten dead found and perhaps fifty wounded on June 10, then eighteen dead found, an estimate of 25-30 killed and 150 wounded, and an enemy acknowledgment of 175 killed and wounded. Pierce reports 21 casualties from the night firing between Union columns and refers to his former report for the rest.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The night-firing casualties belong to the approach march; they overlap any Union total and must not be added to it.

open_questions: Butler's June 10 and June 16 reports and casualty table (No. 1), Townsend's, Bendix's and Kilpatrick's reports, and D.H. Hill's, Stuart's, Randolph's, Montague's and Werth's reports remain deferred; Pierce's 'former report' of losses is not in the inspected pages.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Pierce's June 12, 1861 report (Army Official Records Series I, Volume II) is one family of interested Union accounts. Magruder's June 10 and June 12, 1861 dispatches and report (same volume) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Army and Navy Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and reprints of a report in the other compilation are copies. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner history narrates this engagement; Nicolay's The Outbreak of Rebellion mentions Great Bethel only in passing.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
